belief: Being tempted is the same as sinning.
meta: A Christian look at the false belief that being tempted is the same as sinning, with Scripture, questions, and homework for replacing it with the truth.
origins: Teaching that every unwanted thought or desire is a sin. A sensitive conscience that treats passing thoughts as moral failures. Shame about sexual or angry thoughts that appear without choice. Not understanding the difference between a thought entering the mind and choosing to dwell on it or act on it. Anxiety that makes intrusive thoughts feel more serious.
teaches: Jesus was tempted in every way we are, yet He was without sin. Temptation itself is not sin. James describes the process: desire can lure us, and when it is welcomed and acted on, it gives birth to sin. Temptation is common to everyone, and God is faithful to provide a way out. The battle is not to never be tempted, but to turn to God and resist when temptation comes.
self_statements: Having that thought means I’ve already sinned.
A good Christian would never be tempted like this.
I’m disgusting for even thinking that.
Since I’ve already sinned in my mind, I might as well act on it.
God is angry every time I’m tempted.
errors: Treating a passing thought as the same as a chosen act.
Believing that if you are tempted, you have already failed.
Calling yourself disgusting because a thought appeared.
Concluding “I already sinned, so I might as well act on it.”
questions: Was Jesus tempted? Did He sin?
According to James, when does temptation become sin?
Did I choose this thought, or did it just appear?
What did I do when the temptation came?
Does God promise to take away temptation, or to provide a way out?
Is telling myself I already sinned making it easier to give in?
What way of escape is available to me right now?
truth: Being tempted is not the same as sinning. Jesus was tempted in every way, yet He did not sin. A thought or desire that comes to me is not a sin; it becomes sin when I welcome it and act on it. God is faithful, He will not let me be tempted beyond what I can bear, and He provides a way out.
hw_questions: Was Jesus tempted? Did He sin?
Did I choose this thought, or did it appear?
What did I do when the temptation came?
What does God promise in temptation?
What way of escape is open to me now?
hw_truths: Being tempted is not the same as sinning.
Jesus was tempted too, and He understands.
God will not let me be tempted beyond what I can bear.
I can turn to God the moment temptation comes.
A passing thought does not define me.
log: Each time I face temptation, write what it was and what way of escape I took, even if it was small.
name_example: No temptation has seized Sarah except what is common to man. And God is faithful; He will not let her be tempted beyond what she can bear. But when she is tempted, He will also provide an escape, so that she can stand up under it.

say, “That’s a temptation, not a sin,” and turn your attention to a useful task.

write down two things you will do the next time a common temptation comes.

prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You that You were tempted in every way and yet without sin. Help me reject the lie that being tempted is the same as sinning. When temptation comes, help me turn to You quickly and take the way out You provide. Thank You for understanding my weakness. In Your name, Amen.
